open_questions: Why odd and even transits alternate deep (605.8 ppm) and shallow (1225 ppm) – spot evolution on this 7.1 d rotator likely, needs ground-based multi-color transit monitoring to confirm achromaticity
Secondary dip at phase 0.5489 (snr 5.534) and strong best_brightening_snr 6.68 – needs high-precision photometry to show it is not a persistent secondary, plus RVs to rule out diluted EB
Centroid never on-target (inconclusive) – high-resolution time-series photometry / spectroscopic follow-up to confirm on-target and mass
dossier.public_summary: A 935 ppm, 3.5-hour dip repeats every 13 days on a small active star with a duration that matches a planet's transit and a size of about 2.4 Earth radii. The flat bottom, duration match and lack of credible neighbour stars outweigh a mild odd-even depth difference and a possible small secondary that can be explained by the star's large spot variability. More photometry and radial velocities can still test it, but a planet is the best explanation now.

reasons.why: Planet-sized radius much below 10 Rearth favours planet over stellar eclipse, undiluted depth 936.7 ppm, rp/rstar 0.03061.

Observed duration 3.499 h vs central 3.364 h ratio 1.04 matches central transit; stellar_radius confirms radius_TIC 0.719933 (Gaia 0.7133858799934387) consistent with duration ratios 1.04 / 1.07, immediately favouring planet over EB geometry.
Flat-bottomed (not V-shaped) with best ingress 0.35, opposite of typical EB or grazing binary, supports planet.

On-target not confirmed but also no evidence off-target; neighbours.could_cause_within_1px 0 and plausible_within_1px 0, brightest neighbour 45.4 arcsec away would need 0.2207 eclipse, inconsistent with 935.1 ppm depth, so neighbour EB cannot be positively identified.
reasons.value: inconclusive (no sector with a clear difference image)

reasons.why: No significant depth change across sectors 2 (1058 ppm), 69 (742 ppm), 70 (878 ppm).

Below strong 4-sigma threshold and transit_depths p_consistent 0.0035249600356007907 shows individual transits alternate deep/shallow, consistent with a spotted rotating star (VARIABLE, amplitude 5895-11913 ppm) not an odd/even binary at 26 d.

Not well above strongest brightening and not at half phase (snr_at_half -2.526), but secondary_over_bump 0.8284 is confounded by large phase-curve amplitude 137.8 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.1474); large star variability and xgboost planet_rank 0.31 with 5 similar planets confirmed as planets favour unocculted spot / instrumental effect over genuine secondary.
